The best universities to study marketing in UK for 2027 are led by the University of Bath, followed by Exeter, Southampton, Leeds and Liverpool in the latest Complete University Guide Marketing subject table.

But the ranking only gets you started.

Bath may suit someone who wants marketing with management and a placement year. Southampton makes a stronger case for students interested in digital marketing and consumer data. Leeds offers a specialist, professionally recognised marketing degree, while a postgraduate applicant may be comparing Warwick, Imperial or LSE instead.

This guide keeps the comparison practical: 2027 ranking, course focus, placement options, professional recognition, entry requirements, tuition fees and career fit.

What the Ranking Doesn't Tell You

A league table cannot tell you which course fits you best.

It may place Bath first overall, but a student focused on digital campaigns and consumer data could reasonably prefer Southampton. Someone who wants professional accreditation may give Leeds, Bristol or Loughborough extra weight. Cost changes the picture again: Loughborough has already confirmed its 2027/28 overseas fee, while several competitors have not.

Placement structures also differ. A university may advertise work experience without offering a full year in industry.

Think about it this way: ranking tells you where to start looking; course structure tells you where you may actually thrive.

That distinction matters more than moving one or two places up a table.

Top 10 Universities to Study Marketing in UK

1. University of Bath

Bath ranks first for Marketing in the Complete University Guide 2027, a position its School of Management says it has held continuously since 2017.

Course: Management with Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAA or A*AB

2027/28 international fee: TBC

Placement/recognition: Four-year work-placement route; placements are real jobs and are usually paid

Best for: marketing with strong management foundations.

Bath is particularly useful if you want to understand marketing alongside finance, operations, analytics and wider business decisions. That breadth can pay off later in product marketing, brand management or commercial strategy.

2. University of Exeter

Exeter's 2027 Marketing and Management BSc combines consumer behaviour, branding, marketing communications, research and strategic digital marketing with broader management study.

Course: Marketing and Management BSc

Typical entry: AAB; contextual offer BBB

Latest international fee: £24,900 for 2026 entry; 2027 rate TBC

Placement/recognition: Four-year Industrial Experience option

Best for: strategy, management and substantial workplace experience.

Exeter says typical Industrial Experience salaries range from about £19,000 to £23,000, although actual salaries vary. Previous placement organisations include Apple, Adidas, Deloitte, Disney, EY and PwC.

3. University of Southampton

Southampton ranks third for Marketing in CUG 2027 and has one of the clearest digital and data-led course profiles in the top 10.

Course: Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAA

Published international fee: £24,400

Placement/recognition: Paid industrial placement; IDM accredited

Best for: digital marketing, consumer insight and analytics.

Students can build a digital campaign for a real organisation, while the placement route includes at least 32 weeks in industry. Previous placement employers include Apple, BMW, IBM and Disney.

A course does not need “Digital Marketing” in its title to teach digital marketing well.

4. University of Leeds

Leeds offers a specialist Marketing BSc and ranks fourth in the CUG 2027 table.

Course: Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAB

2027/28 international fee: TBC

Placement/recognition: Optional work placement; CIM accredited

Best for: a focused marketing degree with professional recognition.

The programme is designed for students heading into a digitally driven marketing environment, with later career routes including brand, product marketing, social media, SEO and marketing analytics.

Leeds also offers a major student city without London's cost profile. If budget is part of the decision, compare living costs between UK student locations.

5. University of Liverpool

Liverpool's Marketing BA has been updated for 2027 entry, including closer employer links, digital tools and greater emphasis on research skills.

Course: Marketing BA

Typical entry: AAB

Published international fee: £27,000 for 2026/27; 2027/28 may change

Placement/recognition: Separate four-year Year in Industry route available

Best for: branding, market research, consumer behaviour and analytics.

Modules include consumer behaviour, strategic brand communications, market research and digital analytics.

That breadth makes Liverpool a sensible choice if you know you want marketing but have not yet decided whether brand, digital, research or analytics will become your strongest area.

6. University of Strathclyde

Strathclyde is the highest-ranked Scottish university in the CUG top 10 for Marketing.

Course: BA Marketing

Typical entry: ABB–BBB at A level

Published international fee: £22,750

Placement/recognition: Employer-led projects and business-development opportunities

Best for: a strong Scottish option with a comparatively lower published fee.

Its programme sits in a business-school environment and includes areas such as international business, sustainability and marketing practice.

The current fee is several thousand pounds below some other top-10 options. Over three or four years, that difference stops looking small.

7. Durham University

Durham's undergraduate programme is now structured as BSc Marketing and Management, with the typical A-level entry requirement updated to AAB.

Course: BSc Marketing and Management

Typical entry: AAB

2027/28 international fee: Check the latest published rate

Placement/recognition: Placement-year options available within Durham's business programmes

Best for: students who want marketing within a broader management education.

This route makes sense if you see marketing as part of a wider commercial career rather than a standalone creative discipline.

Product marketers, consultants and commercial managers often spend as much time with finance, sales and strategy teams as they do with advertising teams.

8. University of Bristol

Bristol's 2027 Marketing BSc covers digital marketing, consumer behaviour, branding and the relationship between marketing and wider business decisions.

Course: Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAA; contextual offer ABB

International fee: £28,200 quoted for 2026 entry; 2027 rate TBC

Placement/recognition: CIM and IDM accredited; study-abroad route available

Best for: digital marketing, branding and consumer behaviour.

Bristol stands out for professional recognition: the standard Marketing BSc carries both CIM and IDM accreditation.

It also brings marketing practitioners into the programme alongside academic researchers, which gives the course a useful industry-facing element.

9. Loughborough University

Loughborough offers one of the clearest combinations of marketing specialisation, professional recognition and placement experience.

Course: Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAB

2027/28 international fee: £25,950

Placement/recognition: Four-year placement route; professionally accredited

Best for: employability, digital marketing and students who want a confirmed 2027 budget.

The programme covers digital marketing, consumer behaviour and global brand management alongside wider business skills.

Loughborough also has a practical advantage right now: its £25,950 international fee is already confirmed for 2027/28 while several competing universities still show TBC.

10. University of Birmingham

Birmingham completes the CUG 2027 top 10 and gives practical work a prominent place in its Marketing BSc.

Course: Marketing BSc

Typical entry: AAB

2027/28 international fee: Check the latest published rate

Placement/recognition: Year in Industry available; CIM and DMI accredited

Best for: digital marketing, analytics and live client work.

The Marketing in Action module includes a real client consultancy project, while the curriculum explores digital and data-driven marketing.

That gives students something more useful than another theoretical case study: work they can discuss with an employer.

There is a mildly counterintuitive point here.

A broader marketing-and-management degree can sometimes be the stronger preparation for a marketing career. Brand and product marketers routinely work across customer data, finance, sales, pricing and business strategy.

If you are still choosing between subjects, compare marketing with other strong UK degree options before narrowing your university list.

Best Universities for Undergraduate Marketing

For the best undergraduate marketing programmes in the UK, first decide how specialised you want the degree to be.

Southampton, Leeds, Liverpool, Bristol, Loughborough and Birmingham offer clearly specialist marketing routes.

Bath, Exeter and Durham place marketing within a wider management education.

Then narrow the list by your priorities. Southampton is particularly attractive for digital and data-led marketing. Bath, Exeter, Southampton and Loughborough deserve attention if a placement year matters. Leeds, Bristol, Loughborough and Birmingham become stronger options if professional recognition is important.

The best university on paper and the best course for your career do not always turn out to be the same place.

International qualifications are assessed separately. English-language requirements also vary, so check how universities may assess your English evidence instead of assuming every course applies the same IELTS rule.

For most undergraduate courses, the 2027 UCAS equal-consideration deadline is 13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time.

If UCAS is new to you, prepare the application process before choosing your final five options.

How to Choose the Best Marketing Degree

Start with five questions.

Does the course teach the marketing you want? Look for digital marketing, consumer behaviour, brand management, market research and marketing analytics in the depth that suits your goals.

Can you gain real experience? Check whether the university offers a full placement year, shorter projects or only optional work experience.

Is the specific degree professionally recognised? CIM, IDM or DMI accreditation can be useful, but always verify it for the exact programme.

What will the whole degree cost? Combine tuition with accommodation and everyday living expenses.

And finally, where do you want the degree to take you?

Someone aiming for marketing analytics could reasonably prefer Southampton to a university one place higher. Someone who wants broader commercial training may prefer Bath or Exeter.

Use the ranking to reduce the list.

Use the course to make the decision.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which university is best for marketing in the UK?

The University of Bath ranks first in the Complete University Guide 2027 Marketing subject table, followed by Exeter and Southampton. The best personal choice can still depend on modules, placement opportunities, professional accreditation, cost and career goals.

What are the top marketing universities in the UK for 2027?

The CUG 2027 top 10 are Bath, Exeter, Southampton, Leeds, Liverpool, Strathclyde, Durham, Bristol, Loughborough and Birmingham.

Which universities are best for undergraduate marketing?

Bath, Exeter, Southampton, Leeds and Liverpool lead the current CUG table. Southampton stands out for digital and data-led marketing, while Bath and Exeter suit students who want marketing combined with broader management.

Which UK universities are good for business and marketing?

Bath, Exeter and Durham are particularly useful comparisons if you want marketing alongside wider management and commercial study.

Which university is best for digital marketing?

Southampton is one of the strongest undergraduate options for digital and data-driven marketing. Bristol, Loughborough and Birmingham also combine marketing with digital, analytical or consumer-focused study.

What are the best UK universities for a Master's in Marketing?

Warwick, Imperial, LSE, Manchester and Bath are strong options to compare. Postgraduate applicants should compare specialist programmes rather than relying on an undergraduate subject ranking.

How much does a marketing degree cost in the UK for international students?

Among the universities covered here, current or latest published undergraduate international fees are commonly around £23,000–£29,000 per year. Several 2027/28 fees remain unconfirmed.

Is a placement year worth it for marketing?

Often, yes. Marketing employers value evidence of real work: campaigns, client projects, research, analytics and commercial decision-making. A good placement can give you that evidence before graduation.

Final Thoughts

The best universities to study marketing in UK for 2027 begin with Bath, Exeter, Southampton, Leeds and Liverpool, followed by Strathclyde, Durham, Bristol, Loughborough and Birmingham.

Bath is the strongest starting point if you want marketing with management and a structured placement route. Southampton stands out for digital marketing and consumer data. Leeds offers a specialist CIM-accredited degree. Bristol combines digital and consumer-focused study with CIM and IDM recognition, while Loughborough offers both a placement route and a confirmed £25,950 international fee for 2027/28.

For Master's study, the picture changes. Warwick, Imperial and LSE become much more important comparisons.

Use rankings to build the shortlist. Then compare the course, placement, professional recognition and total cost.

That is where the right choice usually becomes clear.

If you want another view before applying, you can talk through your shortlist with an adviser.
